text: I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned gait and limb ataxia along with a significant medical history; could you please specify your age, the duration of these symptoms, and any relevant past medical conditions or neurological history?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; do you notice any worsening of your symptoms over time, and do you have a known family history of similar neurological issues or conditions like Multiple Sclerosis? Also, have you experienced any recent infections, head trauma, or new medications?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy. Given your history of Crohn's disease and treatment with natalizumab, which carries a known risk for PML, your presentation of gait and limb ataxia is highly concerning for this opportunistic infection affecting the white matter of the brain. I am requesting an MRI of the brain to confirm this diagnosis immediately.
